analysis.title: Tactical Equity Trading Alert: Closing Freeport-McMoRan Inc. (FCX US)
key_insights: Bank J. Safra Sarasin's Wealth Equity Competence Center is closing its TETA trade idea on Freeport-McMoRan (FCX US) ahead of its US$52 stop-loss. The reasons given are broad commodity liquidation, worsening macro conditions and momentum selling.

The Bloomberg Commodity Total Return Index is down 8.2% so far in November and copper is down 11% this month. The report attributes this to a stronger US dollar, rising US Treasury yields and growing expectations of additional Fed rate hikes against persistent inflation.

Post-US midterm election uncertainty over the pace of AI and data center rollouts has weakened one of the main bullish demand narratives for industrial metals. Investors are locking in profits early ahead of year-end.

CTAs and hedge funds are cutting exposure and moving outright short into price weakness, which amplifies the downturn. The report says financial liquidation is currently overpowering fundamental support and is likely to prevent a near-term rebound until macro sentiment stabilizes.

Long-term structural drivers for copper (electrification, grid expansion, tight physical supply in China) are described as intact. The desk will watch FCX for a cleaner re-entry point once rate expectations and systematic selling pressure subside.
The FCX TETA trade was initiated 28-Oct-26 and closed 18-Nov-26 at a return of -16.97% against -5.20% for the MXNA benchmark, a difference of -11.76%.
The report's trade list shows open TETA ideas on Murata Mfg (6981 JP, initiated 16-Sep-26), Oracle (ORCL US, 08-Sep-26), Credo Technology (CRDO US, 28-Aug-26) and Ferrari (RACE IM, 03-Jul-26).

market_movers.rationale: The trade idea is closed ahead of the US$52 stop-loss for a -16.97% return. The stock keeps its Outperform rating in the security details table, and the desk will look for a cleaner re-entry once rate expectations and systematic selling subside.

sector_views.rationale: Commodity liquidation and momentum selling are currently overpowering the structural copper demand drivers. The report expects no near-term rebound until macro sentiment stabilizes.

earnings_insights: FCX expected reporting date is 22.01.2027 per the security details table. No EPS or revenue estimates are given.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Broad commodity liquidation, tied in the report to a stronger dollar, higher Treasury yields and momentum selling.
Copper fell more than the broad commodity index, which pressured FCX toward its stop-loss.
Growing market expectations of Fed hikes against persistent inflation are cited as a driver of the commodity selloff.

trade_ideas.description: Close the long FCX US tactical trade idea ahead of the US$52 stop-loss, for a -16.97% return since the 28-Oct-26 initiation.
trade_ideas.rationale: Commodity liquidation, macro headwinds and momentum selling are overwhelming near-term fundamentals, so closing preserves capital.
trade_ideas.risk: Copper's structural drivers remain intact, so a re-entry may be warranted once rates and systematic selling stabilize.

risk_factors: A stronger US dollar and rising US Treasury yields.
Possible additional Fed rate hikes against persistent inflation.
Uncertainty after the US midterm elections over the pace of AI and data center buildout.
Systematic selling by CTAs and hedge funds moving outright short.
vol_and_positioning: CTAs and hedge funds are cutting exposure and moving outright short in commodities. The report describes this systematic, momentum-driven liquidation as amplifying the copper and FCX decline.
geopolitical: Post-US midterm election uncertainty over the pace of future AI and data center rollouts is cited as weighing on the industrial metals demand narrative.
